name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Publish a *public changelog* for every Kaedim tool update. This forces us to keep links fresh and visible—no hidden changes, no stale docs. The trade-off: we expose internal fixes publicly, but that pressure keeps us honest and speeds up fixes.

name: Scriv
text: Publishing every internal fix risks turning the changelog into noise—users won’t distinguish critical updates from noise, and competitors will exploit our transparency to cherry-pick weaknesses. Instead, ship a *public-facing* changelog that only surfaces user-facing changes, paired with an internal log for engineering; this keeps pressure on freshness without exposing vulnerabilities. Settle it by running a 2-week trial: compare user confusion metrics and competitor exploit attempts before committing.
